description: Original PRD/timeline V1 capability inventory. Actor/capability/source are source-derived or explicitly identified reconstruction; components, dependencies and acceptance are prospective design, not executed historical tests. Scenario coverage is specified in acceptance-cases.json.

requirements.source: PRD p. 2 §2.2, Student Login; p. 5 student flow / login
requirements.acceptance: A valid student can authenticate and reach their own workspace before any class enrollment; class-specific private data remains inaccessible until membership is granted. Missing, expired or invalid student sessions cannot read private data or mutate professor resources.

requirements.source: PRD p. 2 §2.2, Professor Login; p. 5 professor flow / login
requirements.acceptance: A valid professor enters only their authorized workspace. Missing, expired or invalid professor sessions are server-denied before class creation or resource writes with no state change or disclosure; student-role attempts at professor writes are also server-denied with no state change.

requirements.source: PRD p. 2 §2.2, Generate Unique Class Code; p. 5 professor flow / class-code issue
requirements.acceptance: Two independently created classes each receive a usable code; generated codes are distinct and resolve only to their own classes; a code does not itself authorize resource access.

requirements.capability: Look up and validate a class code
requirements.source: PRD p. 2 §2.2, Search for Class Code; p. 5 student flow / search
requirements.acceptance: Valid issued code resolves only to the intended class join target; unknown or invalid codes reveal no private classroom metadata or resource content. Code revocation and renewal are proposed future lifecycle controls, not V1 acceptance prerequisites.

requirements.source: PRD p. 2 §2.2, Join Class; p. 5 student flow / join
requirements.acceptance: Eligible student acquires one membership in the intended class; repeat join remains idempotent and does not grant membership elsewhere.

requirements.source: PRD p. 2 §2.2, Upload Course Materials; p. 5 professor flow / upload
requirements.acceptance: Authorized professor stores a readable document in the owned class; invalid uploads and cross-class requests cause neither resource creation nor leakage.

requirements.source: PRD p. 2 §2.2, Store Course Outline; p. 5 professor flow / outline
requirements.acceptance: Authorized professor can save and retrieve an outline scoped to the correct classroom.

requirements.source: PRD p. 2 §2.2, Store Exams & Quizzes; p. 5 professor flow / Exam & Quiz Data Stored; p. 3 §2.3 defers on-platform quizzes
requirements.acceptance: Professor can save and retrieve exam/quiz information or related material scoped to a classroom; no live student quiz or official grade is inferred.

requirements.source: PRD p. 2 §2.2, Store Textbook Topics; p. 5 professor flow / topics
requirements.acceptance: Authorized professor can save and retrieve multiple class-scoped textbook topic entries without assuming an ordering or reordering control.

requirements.capability: Choose skip-upload branch during class creation
requirements.source: PRD p. 2 §2.2, Skip Upload & Create Empty Class; p. 5 professor flow / skip upload
requirements.acceptance: Professor creates a usable new class via the no-initial-upload option with zero class resource records; this is an alternate R18 creation path, not a second creation operation.

requirements.source: PRD p. 2 §2.2, Professor Dashboard / Assignments Download; p. 5 professor flow / download
requirements.acceptance: Authorized professor downloads a class-owned synthetic homework/test/essay resource with matching bytes; another class owner is denied. Planned assignment/test generation in Week 4 is recorded as ambiguous and unverified.

requirements.source: PRD p. 3 §2.2, AI Chatbot Pre-initialization; p. 5 student flow / preinitialize
requirements.acceptance: Authenticated enrolled student starts tutor interaction bound to the intended class even if that class has no uploaded teaching materials.

requirements.source: PRD p. 3 §2.2, Choose Q&A or Concept Bot; p. 5 student flow / mode
requirements.acceptance: Both AI modes are selectable for the same enrolled classroom without changing membership or permitting cross-class access.

requirements.capability: Supply authorized subject data to Q&A
requirements.source: PRD p. 3 §2.2, Retrieve Subject Data; p. 5 student flow / subject document
requirements.acceptance: Healthy Q&A obtains readable authorized class-specific content; empty/missing/denied contexts yield separate, nonleaking outcomes.

requirements.source: PRD p. 3 §2.2, Answer Subject-Based Questions; p. 5 student flow / response
requirements.acceptance: Healthy Q&A conveys class-specific synthetic canary with supporting permitted-source evidence and no-context and swapped-class controls; simulated provider outage fails safely.

requirements.capability: Explain concept and provide three practice problems
requirements.source: PRD p. 3 §2.2, Explain Concepts & Provide Practice Problems; p. 5 student flow / 3 practice problems
requirements.acceptance: Concept mode presents a mathematically sound explanation and a distinct three-problem practice set, reflecting the source diagram; no upload is required for this proposed fixture.

requirements.source: PRD p. 3 §2.2, Evaluate Answers; p. 5 student flow / retry, next concept
requirements.acceptance: Incorrect answer produces accurate feedback and retry; correct answer enables progression; outage preserves state; no official grade is recorded.

requirements.source: PRD p. 5 professor flow / New Class and Select Existing Class branches; timeline Week 3 dashboard plan
requirements.acceptance: A professor creates a classroom exactly once with correct owner; normal and skip-upload branches are alternative choices within the same creation operation. In a fresh authenticated session, the owner can reopen that existing class and retrieve unchanged saved resources; a different professor cannot select the class or read its private resources.
